beamHold.error.generic: The beam hold check could not be completed.
beamHold.error.hardwareUnavailable: The beam hold could not reach the hardware. Check the Glasgow connection and service status.
beamHold.externalControl: Take control of scan and blanking
beamHold.hint: Holds the takeover of the scan Run would start (same frames, frame time and Frame blank) with the beam parked, and records the detector. It ends with its last frame, like the scan. With the beam parked the trace should be flat: dark dips on a fixed period mean something outside our scan is blanking the beam. Turning this on starts immediately.
beamHold.mock: Mock data: synthetic dips, not the instrument
beamHold.observeOnly: Observe only: the instrument keeps its own scan and blanker. Use this to record the instrument's behaviour for comparison.
beamHold.productionOnly: Beam hold takes over the instrument, so it runs only when scans use the hardware: IsProduction = true, or simulation switched off.
beamHold.traceHint: Detector signal over time with the beam parked. Shaded: lowest value per column, so short dips stay visible. Red marks: detected dips.
beamHold.verdict.blanked: Beam held blanked: expect a flat, dark trace. Any bright rise means the beam is getting through our blank.
beamHold.verdict.clean: No dips: the parked beam stayed steady. Blanking is fully under our control.
beamHold.verdict.irregular: Dips found, but not on a fixed period. Check the detector and cabling, then repeat.
beamHold.verdict.periodic: Periodic dips every ~{spacing} ms while we hold the blank: the instrument's own blanking is still reaching the beam. Probe the blank-enable relay (A4/A5) and the blanker input now.
beamHold.verdict.periodicObserve: Periodic dips every ~{spacing} ms with the instrument in control. Repeat with "Take control" on: if they disappear, the takeover works.
beamHold.verdict.tooShort: Recording; the analysis starts after about 0.3 s.
beamHold.verdict.tooShortDone: Too short to judge: this scan's takeover is under 0.3 s. Raise Repeat (Vector) or the resolution so the hold lasts at least 1 s; dips every ~195 ms need several periods.

settings.pins.group.controlHint: Six bus strobes the BusController FSM generates. An empty pin string keeps the FPGA-internal signal toggling for FakeAdcSimulator while emitting no Resource constraint.
settings.pins.group.dataHint: Shared 14-bit bidirectional bus. Pin string is space-separated, LSB-first. An empty string emits no Resource and lets the internal data lines drive the loopback adapter.
settings.pipeline.body: Maximum number of scan-command chunks the sender can queue ahead of received data. Default: 8. Choose a preset or a custom integer from 1 to 128. Smaller values reduce queued work, so live Zoom and ROI changes can reach the hardware sooner, but may introduce scan pauses if the command queue empties. Larger values can keep scanning smoother but delay geometry changes. Start with 8 and compare responsiveness and image continuity on your hardware; the delay also depends on chunk size and dwell time. Click Update to save and restart the service. The setting applies to the next scan; changing it does not resize the current scan pipeline.
settings.pipeline.help: Advanced: default 8. Reduce it for more responsive live Zoom. Smaller values reduce queued scan time but may introduce pauses. Save and restart applies this to the next scan.
